verdict: NOT READY TO FREEZE (check-pigment, A15, read-only, 4.3 min: start 1792325078, end 1792325336). In tripo_rebuild\pigment_project.py, the z-buffer, the 2 px mask erosion, the E5 skin/hair split, and the per-kind mirroring with per-part limits all look sound. Units and frames are consistent: limits in m, mirror distances in mm, depth_mm/1000, head frame mm = head_local*1000. No Tripo colours are read, and Tripo's npz has only v, f and note. No Phase 1 OPEN number is used as a reference: the inputs are the eyes.json iris centres, the nose.json leather outline (checked) and the ears pink band through coat_field. The tool is not trustworthy yet for four reasons. (1) The camera it depends on is not frozen. (2) The tool's own frame check and round-trip probe are circular, and they cannot fail on the errors they exist to catch. (3) Its E5 and Tripo-colour guards can never fail. (4) It has no rule for surfaces the photo can never see: Henry's pocket slot (C6b), nostril cavities and the ear canal. It was tested only on Tripo and on skin.npz, both of which have blind nostril dishes and no slot, so it cannot have seen this. My own held-out check through the registered camera: the ear tips land 5.6 px (L) and 8.6 px (R) off, which is about 2.1 / 3.2 mm at 0.375 mm/px. The fitted points land 1.7 / 4.0 / 6.1 px off. Paw floor contacts land 7-16 px off, mostly vertically, and that offset partly comes from how the points are defined.
blocking: CAMERA NOT FROZEN: camera_frozen.json is in the Rodin canonical frame (Tripo silhouette IoU 0.52). Every output depends on an unfrozen test file (%TEMP%\p2prep_pigment\tripo100k\camera_registered.json: rotvec (-1.66,-0.28,3.80) deg, t (-19.9,105.9,-1.7) mm). The orchestrator or the person must freeze one camera before any pigment value is used.

FRAME CHECK IS CIRCULAR: after --register, frame_check re-measures silhouette IoU against the same ref_mask.png the registration maximised (pigment_project.py line 253 vs lines 547-549; 0.9146 reported as proof of frame). Held-out photo points exist in ref_points.json (chin, ear_tip.L/R, fpaw/hpaw x4) and are never used. My held-out projection: ear tips miss by 5.6 / 8.6 px (2.1 / 3.2 mm), worse than the fitted eyes. The freeze must be gated on held-out residuals per part.

ROUND-TRIP PROBE IS BLIND TO REGISTRATION: projecting through camera X and rendering back through the same X reproduces the photo at every directly seen hair pixel, whatever the pose error. So the note 'tests registration' (line 561) is false. A camera shifted 5 mm would still PASS. Needed: planted-failure proofs that FAIL, namely a perturbed camera (markings on the wrong anatomy), a region shifted dE 5, a blurred marking edge and an injected Tripo colour (A12, PHASE2_ROUND0 line 111). Crispness also passes by only 0.03 px at 400k (extra blur 1.467 vs 1.5 limit) and FAILs at 100k (1.823).

GUARDS THAT CANNOT FAIL: the E5 assert (lines 388-391) is a tautology, because skin_rgb is built as NaN off-skin and then asserted NaN off-skin; e5_skin_painted_under_fur is the same test. tripo_colours_read=0 (line 455) is a hard-coded constant. The tool has no planted proofs at all, against the precision-budget rule of strict proofs for engine tools.

NO INTERIOR / NEVER-SEEN CLASS: the mirror fill takes the nearest DIRECT same-kind vertex within 3 mm (head) of the mirrored point, with no normal or same-surface test (lines 358-363). On the Phase 2 mesh this will copy colour across folds and into cavities. The inner wall of Henry's pocket slot (C6b) would take the outer flap's colour. Nostril cavity walls (C6) would take leather colour, or muzzle hair colour once they pass the nose mask's ymax ramp (coat_field.py lines 268-272, which makes them 'hair'). The ear canal (C14, hairless) would get a hair colour or the trace colour. The spec needs an 'interior' class (never photo-filled, colour from anatomy, flagged), and the mirror needs a normal-agreement test.
should: EYE treated as skin pigment on Tripo's eye cap (a quadric, no globe; Phase 1 says the eyeball comes in Phase 2). Photo iris pixels, catchlights included, are baked onto it. On skin400k, eye_opening L vs R median L* is 47.4 vs 37.9, which looks like lighting asymmetry. For C6 globes, iris colour should come from the iris trace with pupil and catchlight excluded, and go on the iris behind the cornea, not on a furless skin mask.

C14 EAR HAIR: inner-ear skin pigment is read inside ear_in traces that also contain furnishing hairs, which are white over the pink skin. inner_ear_pink.L is 30-63 % trace_fill, one flat median. Where furless >= 0.5, hair_rgb is NaN, so sparse inner-pinna hair and furnishings get no colour target. ear_back is only 10-12 % covered, and no fallback is stated for the ear back or for the canal.

C13 WHISKERS: the spec gives no whisker colour target, and whisker pixels are not excluded from hair reads (photo_features.json has no whisker trace). This is harmless on cat1, where the whiskers are white over white muzzle fur, but it is a general engine gap.

G2 SOURCE/CONFIDENCE: hair_targets carry one generic source string, skin_pigment entries carry none, and no value carries a positional uncertainty from registration. The silhouette disagrees by a median of 5 px and a p90 of 15-17 px, about 2-7 mm. Add a per-vertex uncertainty (local silhouette or held-out residual) and a per-region confidence.

PIXEL SCALE: PHASE2_ROUND0 line 48 says '~0.27 mm/px'. Through the registered camera I measure 0.375 mm/px at the ear tips, 0.38-0.42 at the paws and 0.45 at the tail contact. Fix the criterion (it also bears on C5 tolerances) and the MIRROR_MM_PART comment.

REGISTRATION LANDMARK 'nose' is the centroid of the 3D leather outline (line 223), while the photo point (706,377) may be defined differently; its residual is 6.1 px. Match the definitions or drop the point. A single rigid fit to the whole-body silhouette lets the rump and tail (15-17 px off) pull on the head, where the crispest markings are, so consider a head-weighted or per-part fit and report residuals per part.

UNCOVERED 38-40 % with no stated fallback: paw pads 100 %, head_crown 72-77 %, back 63-66 %, ear_back 88-90 %. Stage 5 needs a stated source for each, such as a same-region photo median flagged 'estimate' or cited colour-point anatomy, each with a confidence.

HAIR-LIE OFFSET: the fact that photo tips sit downstream of their roots is recorded as OPEN but not quantified. On the face the forehead stripes are a few mm wide, comparable to the likely offset, so quantify it from coat.json lie lengths before Stage 5.

RESOLUTION: the pre-blur sigma is set from the GLOBAL median projected edge (lines 303-305), so the coarse body mesh blurs the dense face. Per-vertex colour is at its crispness limit even at 400k. Consider a UV texture bake or a local footprint sigma.

MASK FRAME: CF.weights and CF.masks are evaluated on the inset skin v (line 311 assumes depth 0 on furless areas). Near the mask edges, where depth > 0, the furless boundary shifts by the coat depth. Evaluate the masks on the envelope (seen) or document the shift.
